question.prompt: Carlos went to a sports store to buy running shoes. Running shoes were on sale, with prices reduced by \(20\%\) on every pair of shoes. Carlos also knew that he had to pay a \(7.5\%\) sales tax on the discounted price. He had \(43\) dollars. What is the original (before discount) price of the most expensive shoes he could afford to buy?

solutions.title: Apply the discount, then tax
solutions.explanation:
The sales tax applies to the discounted price, so its percentage must be calculated after the discount.

Let \(p\) be the original price in dollars. The \(20\%\) discount leaves \(80\%\) of the original price, or \(0.8p\). Adding \(7.5\%\) tax gives a total cost of
\[
0.8p+0.075(0.8p)=0.8p(1.075)=0.86p.
\]
Carlos can afford the shoes when
\[
0.86p\le43,
\qquad
p\le\frac{43}{0.86}=50.
\]
An original price of \(50\) dollars gives a total cost of exactly \(43\) dollars. Therefore the greatest affordable original price is \(\boxed{50}\) dollars, choice \(\boxed{\text{B}}\).

solutions.title: Test the largest choice
solutions.explanation:
The largest listed original price is \(50\) dollars, and its discount and tax are easy to calculate directly.

At that price, the discount is
\[
20\%\cdot50=10\text{ dollars},
\]
so the discounted price is \(40\) dollars. The sales tax is
\[
7.5\%\cdot40=3\text{ dollars}.
\]
The total is \(40+3=43\) dollars, exactly Carlos's budget. Any higher original price would produce a higher discounted price and a higher total after tax. Thus the maximum original price is \(\boxed{50}\) dollars, choice \(\boxed{\text{B}}\).
